A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowRVS research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support matching retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original RVOS benchmark results, component and VAE ablations, and qualitative segmentation results, including appendix visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and reports revised VAE results plus additional failure cases and an unseen-action example.

M1.justification: Both versions use the Wan 2.1-based video-to-mask flow with BBS, SPA, DVI and separately adapted VAE decoding. New Appendix D specifies existing sampling and channel-concatenation mechanics; it does not establish a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: The RefCOCO/+/g training coverage and three RVOS benchmarks remain unchanged. v2 Appendix C and Figure 9 add a limited test scenario using action phrases absent from MeViS training, illustrated by 'the dog somersaulting.'

E2.justification: Table 3 removes the 'Add Trainable Conv Head' comparator, leaving frozen and fine-tuned VAE decoders. The external baseline membership in Table 1 and alternative paradigms in Table 2 remain unchanged. Newly discussed HCD, REM and ControlNet are not added as evaluated competitors.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark splits, training and zero-shot setup, metrics and Table 4 hyperparameters remain unchanged. Section 3.3 newly documents matched backbone, optimizer, learning rate, duration and VAE controls for existing alternatives. Neither this disclosure nor the revised Table 3 scores establishes a protocol change.

E4.justification: The VAE ablation loses its convolutional-head condition and appendix reconstruction comparison. v2 adds two qualitative failure cases concerning relational actions and temporal ordering, plus an unseen-action generalization example. Existing BBS sensitivity, component and pretrained-weight analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Both retain point estimates and selected qualitative examples.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises frozen-VAE reconstruction/performance from 29.7/19.6 to 98.8/60.0, changes fine-tuned performance from 60.6 to 60.9, and removes the 85.4/53.2 convolutional-head results. Table 2 changes one-step-mask J&F/J/F from 36.2/41.5/38.9 to 38.9/36.2/41.5. New qualitative outcomes include two failures and successful unseen-action segmentation. Table 1 is unchanged; the VAE revisions are not explained as comparable-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds explicit probability-law definitions for BBS and SPA: a point-mass/uniform mixture and sampling from the encoder's Gaussian posterior. These specify distributions previously described verbally. The central flow ODE remains unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its criticism of prior methods: independent-frame processing and coarse geometric bottlenecks become a qualified concern about instance-centric representations, acknowledging conditioned segmentation. The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same flow formulation, adaptation suite and benchmark superiority claims.

C2.justification: The VAE interpretation changes substantially: v1 describes frozen decoding as failing because of domain shift, whereas v2 describes it as competitive and fine-tuning as a 0.9-point refinement. Appendix C adds concrete limitations involving multi-part actions and counting/ordering, and attributes unseen-action success to transferable T2V priors rather than memorization.

D1.justification: Appendix D specifies sampling distributions, SPA's encoder-derived variance, and DVI's doubled input channels and first-convolution adjustment. Section 3.3 discloses common settings for alternative paradigms. Hyperparameters and the abstract's code link remain unchanged, but a new reproducibility statement promises release after acceptance, conflicting with the retained claim that code is available; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for HCD, ReferEverything/REM and ControlNet, distinguishing frozen feature extraction, one-step prediction and externally conditioned generation from FlowRVS. It removes the Peebles and Xie citation. These refine nearby research positioning while retaining the central language-guided flow distinction.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction, related-work and VAE-discussion rewrites, typo corrections, conference and author-note updates, and new acknowledgment, ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements. The appendices are reorganized and expanded, while the main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives drawing and label refinements, and Table 3 loses a row. The VAE reconstruction figure is removed; earlier qualitative Figures 6–8 survive as Figures 5–7 with adjusted placement and sizing. New Figures 8–9 display failures and unseen-action results. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility and critical assessment through explicit component details, matched-baseline disclosures, closer prior-work positioning and concrete failure cases absent from v1. The gains are limited: the main benchmark study is unchanged, the large Table 3 revisions remain unexplained, and Table 2's revised 38.9 J&F still conflicts with the retained 36.2 and +14.6 discussion.
